seatsSat: UX and information design — Orla, venue manager at The Orchard
headline: The first round on a frozen surface, and the first whose worst finding was a live crash. Seven seats drove one page NARROWED across 720 — something no loop in either gate had ever done, because every one of them opens a fresh page per width — and three of them independently hit the same ReferenceError: the media-query listeners the 2 September ledger added had never executed at all, so the timeline kept the desk composition on a phone and Tasks kept a five-lane board in a 372px viewport. Four green gates had frozen that build hours earlier. The round also proved a second blind spot of the same shape: every no-sideways-scroll assertion had only ever run on a coarse pointer, so the dictation floor overflowed the document by 145px at 320 — WCAG 1.4.10 — on exactly the narrowed desktop window the guideline describes. Refutation rose from 14% to 29%: three seats sighted the Timeline wordmark and all three were killed, one by driving rather than reading. 24 confirmed, 7 closed, 17 standing.

confirmed.element: title="Reading a photo happens on another screen. Not here yet." (src/notes.js:1675, 1698, 1800) and title="Notes options are on another screen. Not here yet." (src/notes.js:1633) against the ratified NOT_YET grammar at src/app.js:96-105; ELSEWHERE at src/notes.js:3462-3469
confirmed.problem: The honest doors were settled in one grammar and Notes' own two closed doors did not get it. src/app.js:96-105 holds five noun phrases naming a destination — "Every project in one list. Not here yet.", "Guides and support. Not here yet." — with the reason recorded in the code (a door's job is to name what is behind it). Notes' photo and options doors instead say the work "happens on another screen", which names a place this product does not have and tells Orla her photo-reading is somewhere else rather than not built. Driven, the same voice reaches the screen reader five more times (src/notes.js:3462-3469). One of those five is broken English: ELSEWHERE.privacy at src/notes.js:3465 concatenates N.copy.privacyLong, which has no terminal period, so pressing "Private to you" announces "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — two sentences fused with no punctuation. The same token is concatenated correctly, with the period, at src/notes.js:2656.
confirmed.fix: Correct two errors in the proposed fix first. (a) ELSEWHERE.photo and ELSEWHERE.options are DEAD code: src/notes.js:3220 intercepts any aria-disabled control whose title matches /Not here yet/ and announces the TITLE — driven, [data-act="options"] and [data-act="photo"] speak their titles verbatim and never reach the table. So rewrite the titles at 1633/1675/1698/1800 and delete those two table entries rather than rewriting them. (b) ELSEWHERE.more is reached ONLY by the note-level button at src/notes.js:1951/2200, whose own aria-label is "More actions for this note" — the suite door is handled separately at src/notes.js:3243 — so it must become "More for this note. Not here yet.", NOT "The rest of Signal Studio. Not here yet." as proposed, which would keep the exact mismatch that makes it a defect. Then: titles 1633 -> "More for this note. Not here yet."; 1675/1698/1800 -> "A photo, read into words. Not here yet."; ELSEWHERE.privacy -> `${N.copy.privacyLong}. Your privacy settings. Not here yet.` (the period is the bug); retry -> "Sending again. Not here yet. Your note is still here."; destroy -> "Deleting for good. Not here yet. Nothing here is deleted.". Gate it: assert every string a closed door speaks ends in "Not here yet." (optionally plus one reassurance sentence) and that no string in src/ contains "another screen".
confirmed.verdict: Driven at 1440 on notes.notebook, two of these are objectively broken, not taste: pressing the head's "Private to you" announces into the live region, verbatim, "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — two sentences fused, because N.copy.privacyLong (src/fixture.js:617) has no terminal period and src/notes.js:3465 omits the one that lines 1632 and 2656 both add; and pressing the note's "More actions for this note" announces "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen.", the wrong destination and with no "Not here yet." at all. src/notes.js is the only file in src/ containing "another screen" (11 occurrences) against the ratified noun-phrase grammar at src/app.js:96-105, and the door titles contradict themselves in one breath — "happens on another screen. Not here yet." cannot both be true.

confirmed.element: .b-layout [data-layout-to] / [data-app="timeline"][data-layout] — src/timeline.js:176-178 `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { if (C.rootEl()... ) go("owner-flight"); })`, in the core IIFE that opens at src/timeline.js:26; `C` is only declared at src/timeline.js:331, inside the renderer's separate closure
confirmed.problem: `C` is not in scope at line 177, so every crossing of 720px throws `ReferenceError: C is not defined` (measured: Chromium pageerror at MediaQueryList.<anonymous>, on 768→721→700 and again on 700→900) and the re-mount never runs. The file's own header comment at src/timeline.js:4-8 states the contract this handler exists to keep — "the across composition is withheld on it, and crossing it re-mounts the owner's surface so the bar is never stale" — and it is not kept. Driven: load timeline.owner-flight at 1024 (data-layout="across", the Across/Down group present), resize to 700 → data-layout stays "across" and the Across/Down buttons are still on screen at phone width, against the locked decision "Across is never offered on a phone". `acrossAllowed()` (src/timeline.js:620) reads `!PHONE_T.matches` correctly, but only at render time, and nothing re-renders. The reverse is as bad: load at 700 (down, no toggle), widen to 1024 → still down, toggle still absent, so a desk user who narrowed the window once can never get the across composition back. The gates cannot see any of this because both open a fresh page per viewport and never cross the boundary.
confirmed.fix: Replace the body of the handler at src/timeline.js:177 with a plain re-mount in the scope it actually lives in — `mount();` — and nothing else. Do NOT call `go()`: `go()` (src/timeline.js:2318-2326) moves focus to `.b-pressTitle`/`.b-who`, and stealing focus to a heading because somebody dragged a window edge is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Add the same one-line remount to the tasks/notes pattern already in use (`PHONE.addEventListener("change", () => mount())`, src/tasks.js:4203) so all three products cross 720 the same way, and add one assertion to interaction-check.mjs that resizes an open page across 720 in both directions and requires zero pageerrors plus `[data-layout-to]` absent below 721.
confirmed.verdict: confirmed by reproduction — the failing gate log is panel/round-6/confirmed-by-reproduction/

confirmed.element: [data-app="notes"] .darkActs / .darkAct — src/notes.css:1889 `.darkActs { display: flex; ... flex: 0 0 auto; margin-left: auto; }`, src/notes.css:1007 `.darkAct { ... height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; }`, and src/notes.css:1787 `.darkAct kbd { display: none; }` which lives inside `@media (pointer: coarse)` opened at src/notes.css:1770
confirmed.problem: In notes.voice the dictation overlay's action pair cannot shrink or wrap, so it forces the whole DOCUMENT to scroll sideways. Measured: `.darkActs` renders 440px wide at left:32, needing 472px of viewport; `.darkAct` ("Stop and read it back" + a 63px `<kbd>Ctrl Enter</kbd>`) is 296px with no min-width:0. Driven at height 844: without mobile emulation documentElement overflow is 152px @320, 82px @390, 42px @430, 12px @460, 0 from ~472; WITH the gate's own isMobile/hasTouch emulation it is still 28px @320. The only rule that relieves it hides the keycap under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, so a narrowed desktop window — which is exactly how WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow is tested, and what a 1280px desktop at 400% zoom becomes — never gets it, and neither does a 320px phone. 1.4.10 (AA) requires no two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px; this state fails it in both pointer modes. The gate cannot see it because config.viewports starts at 390 and marks it isMobile, and `@media (max-width: 900px)` at src/notes.css:1893 only lets `.darkFoot` wrap — it never touches `.darkActs`. This is the same class the 2 September ledger already closed once for notes.review ("the one state in the suite that scrolled sideways at 390 was the one the gate never walked"); it is back, one state over.
confirmed.fix: Ship only the first TWO of the three proposed rules, appended after src/notes.css:1899: `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkActs { flex: 1 1 100%; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-left: 0; min-width: 0; } }` and `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkAct { flex: 1 1 100%; min-width: 0; justify-content: center; padding: 0 12px; } }`. Verified with the rules injected at the DOCUMENT TAIL (injecting into <head> loses the same-specificity cascade to the page's own <style> at line 10 and leaves a spurious 26px residual — that, not a second cause, is what the cut-off run saw): overflow is 0px at 320/360/390/430/460/719 in BOTH pointer modes, pills stay 44px tall at 256px @320 and 326px @390, nothing clips, and 768/1440 are unchanged (131/290 fine, 86/215 coarse). Do NOT add the third rule and do NOT delete the coarse keycap hide: without them the keycap still fits unclipped inside the 256px pill at 320 and overflow is still 0, so the Ctrl+Enter hint survives for exactly the keyboard user who narrows a desktop window. Then add { "name": "320x844", "width": 320, "height": 844 } with no isMobile to elevate.config.json so the reflow width is gated on a fine pointer.
confirmed.verdict: Driven and reproduced: on a fine pointer at height 844, notes.voice makes documentElement.scrollWidth exceed clientWidth by 145px @320, 75px @390, 35px @430, 5px @460, 0 from 472, and window.scrollX really moves (scrolled to 60 at 390) — and it is user-reached, not URL-only: at 390 fine-pointer the single visible [data-act="voice"] glyph in the dock takes overflow from 0 to 75px on one click. The only relief is `.darkAct kbd { display: none }` inside `@media (pointer: coarse)` (src/notes.css:1787), so a narrowed desktop window — the exact WCAG 1.4.10 reflow test — never gets it; the gate misses it because interaction-check.mjs open() sets isTouch from vp.isMobile and config.viewports starts at 390 with isMobile:true.

[data-app="notes"] h1.headName / li.idxSection > h3.idxDay — src/notes.js:1628 `

All your notes

`, killed by src/notes.css:1595 `[data-app="notes"] .headName { display: none; }` inside `@media (max-width: 720px)`; the day groups at src/notes.js:2128 `

confirmed.problem: Notes is the only product of the three whose heading outline is wrong, and it is wrong two different ways. At a desk the accessibility tree reads heading[1] "All your notes" followed straight by five heading[3] day groups — level 2 does not exist anywhere in the product, so the outline skips a level on the surface a person spends most of their time on. At ≤720 `display: none` removes the h1 from the tree entirely (display:none prunes, it does not merely hide), so on a phone notes.notebook offers five level-3 headings under nothing, and notes.review offers a lone level-2 "Worth doing something about?" under nothing. Measured with page.accessibility.snapshot at 390 and 1440 across all four Notes states. Tasks keeps h1 "The Orchard, events" (plus five h2 lane names at a desk) at both widths and Timeline keeps h1 "Mara & Finn" plus two h2s at both widths, so this is Notes' defect alone, not a suite decision. The gate cannot see it: interaction-check.mjs never inspects heading levels, and the audit does not model the accessibility tree.
confirmed.fix: Both edits verified inert. (1) In the ≤720 block replace `[data-app="notes"] .headName { display: none; }` with the sheet's existing `.sr` treatment from src/shell.css:89 AND add `min-width: 0` — the base rule at src/notes.css:287 sets `min-width: 5ch`, which would otherwise fight `width: 1px`. Driven at 390 in all four Notes states, before vs after: .head stays 100px tall and 372px wide, its bottom stays at y=109, .idx top is unchanged (224/194/142/224), documentElement X-overflow stays 0 and scrollHeight is unchanged — the only delta is the tree gaining its root. (2) Emit `<h2 class="idxDay">` at src/notes.js:2128 and drop role/aria-level: notes.css contains NO tag-based heading selector at all, and a live h3→h2 swap at 1440 left all five .idxDay boxes byte-identical in x/y/width/height/font-size/weight/colour/tracking/padding/position, with the outline becoming 1,2,2,2,2,2. Add one gate assertion per state per width: an h1 is present in the tree and no level is skipped.
confirmed.verdict: Enumerated the live outline in all four Notes states at 1440 and 390: at 1440 notes.notebook/notes.voice read h1 "All your notes" then five h3.idxDay with no h2 anywhere, and at 390 src/notes.css:1595 `display:none` prunes h1.headName from the tree entirely, leaving notes.notebook/voice as five orphan h3s, notes.review as a lone h2, and notes.seam with ZERO headings in the accessibility tree. Tasks keeps h1 at both widths and Timeline keeps h1+two h2s at both widths, so this is Notes alone; interaction-check.mjs never inspects heading levels.

confirmed.element: PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", …) — _gate-suite.html:20190-20192, `C.rootEl()` inside the IIFE that spans _gate-suite.html:20040-20319, where `C` is never declared (`var C = window.__TLCORE` is at _gate-suite.html:20345, inside the NEXT IIFE)
confirmed.problem: Every crossing of the 720px phone query throws `Uncaught ReferenceError: C is not defined` at _gate-suite.html:20191, in all three products (reproduced by resizing tasks.board, notes.notebook and timeline.owner-flight from 1440 to 720 — one throw each, in both directions). The handler's whole job is to re-render the timeline for the new layout, so it does nothing at all. The consequence is measured: timeline.owner-flight loaded fresh at 390 gives data-layout="down", zero layout toggles and the action bar folded to "Add a moment · ···". The SAME state narrowed from 1440 to 390 gives data-layout="across", TWO visible [data-layout-to] buttons and the full desk bar "Add a moment / Preview / Get the link" — so the phone gets the across composition and the layout toggle that the 2 September ledger decided is never offered on a phone, plus a three-button desk bar at 390. Enlarging back does not repair it either; the state is stuck at whatever the first paint chose. The behaviour gate cannot see this: it opens each state fresh at a fixed viewport and never resizes, and document overflow stays 0 so the sideways-scroll assertions stay green. A person rotating a phone, a tablet entering split view, or anyone dragging a browser window narrower gets this surface.
confirmed.fix: Two lines. In the IIFE at _gate-suite.html:20040, add `var C = window.__TLCORE;` beside the other module handles at the top of that IIFE (or replace the reference at :20191 with `window.__TLCORE.rootEl()`), so the handler runs instead of throwing. Then, because the handler currently re-renders only when the state is owner-flight, widen it to re-render whatever is mounted: `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { var st = window.__TLCORE.rootEl().getAttribute("data-state"); if (st) go(st); });`. Add to interaction-check.mjs a resize assertion for every state and every crossing: open at 1440, setViewportSize to 390 and back, and require (a) pageErrors unchanged, and (b) that the post-resize DOM matches a fresh load at that width on data-layout, the count of visible [data-layout-to], and the visible .b-act labels.
confirmed.verdict: confirmed by reproduction — the failing gate log is panel/round-6/confirmed-by-reproduction/

confirmed.element: `let view = matchMedia("(max-width: 1099px)").matches ? "list" : "board";` — _gate-suite.html:11496, read once at script parse and never given a `change` listener (compare the 720 query at _gate-suite.html:11507-11509, which does get one)
confirmed.problem: The board/list rule is evaluated exactly once, at load. tasks.board loaded fresh at 390 correctly opens the List (segmented control reads "Board, List*", zero lanes rendered, board scrollWidth 372 = clientWidth). The same state narrowed from 1440 to 390 stays on the Board: five lanes visible and a board whose scrollWidth is 1520px inside a 372px viewport — a five-lane kanban paging sideways on a phone, which is the surface the 2 September ledger decided against ("below 1100 the board is a LIST"). It never repairs: enlarging and re-narrowing leaves it wherever the first paint put it. Document overflow stays 0 because the board is its own scroller, so every sideways-scroll assertion stays green, and the gate never resizes, so 129 assertions cannot see it.
confirmed.fix: Promote the query to a live one, matching what the 720 query already does. Replace the one-shot read with `const LIST_Q = matchMedia("(max-width: 1099px)"); let view = LIST_Q.matches ? "list" : "board"; let viewChosen = false;` — set `viewChosen = true` in the segmented control's handler at _gate-suite.html:14575 so an explicit human choice is never overridden — then `LIST_Q.addEventListener("change", (e) => { if (viewChosen) return; const next = e.matches ? "list" : "board"; if (next === view) return; view = next; mount(); });`. mount() already restores scroll and focus, so no place-keeping work is needed. Cover it in interaction-check.mjs with the same fresh-vs-resized comparison the crossing finding asks for: at 390 require the List selected and zero .tray sections rendered whether the width was arrived at by loading or by resizing.
confirmed.verdict: confirmed by reproduction — the failing gate log is panel/round-6/confirmed-by-reproduction/

confirmed.element: [data-app="tasks"] .lrow { align-items: center } at _gate-suite.html:1611, overriding [data-app="tasks"] .lrows { align-items: start } at :1600 — the default view below 1100 and the phone's only view
confirmed.problem: The row is a five-column subgrid in which one column is top-aligned and four float to the row's vertical middle, so a row has no shared first line. Measured on row one ('Confirm marquee sides with the hire company' + a three-line note) at 768x1024: .lrowTitle's first line centres at y=241.8, while .tick, .lrowLane ('TO DO'), .lrowWho ('Mara & Finn') and .lrowMeta all centre at y=280.5 — 38.7px lower, level with line two of the note. The offset is a function of note length, not a constant: 38.7px on that row, 20.3px on a two-line row at 1050, 0px on a single-line row, and 38.7px for the tick at 390. So the leftmost column of the list — thirteen circles down the page — wobbles by up to 39px against the titles they tick, and reading across a row you pass a title, then a note, then meet the lane and the owner two lines below where the row began. It is also the one alignment declaration in this file with no comment defending it. Nothing here needs invention: the parent already declares `align-items: start`.
confirmed.fix: Ship the two lines exactly as proposed and add nothing. Driven at 1050/768/390: max |tick centre − title first-line centre| goes 21.3/40.1/40.1 -> 1.0px and the spread across all thirteen rows goes 20.3/30.2/30.2 -> 0.0px; row heights are byte-identical at 1050 and 768 and the phone list grows 12px in total; the tick's 32px ::before hit area is unaffected; no horizontal overflow appears. Do NOT also restore the tick's `margin-top: 1px` by removing the `.lrow .tick { margin: 0 }` reset at src/tasks.css:506 — tried, and it pushes the offset back out to 2.0px; the existing reset is what makes start-alignment land at 1px. Gate it as the finding says: in every .lrow the centre of .tick must sit within 2px of the centre of .lrowTitle's first line at 1050, 768 and 390.
confirmed.verdict: Measured on the default view below 1100 and the phone's only view: with .lrow { align-items: center } (src/tasks.css:488) the tick's centre sits 39.7px below the centre of its title's first line on row one at 768, and the offset tracks note length rather than being constant — per-row it is 9.9 / 21.3 / 30.7 / 39.7 / 40.1px at 768 and 1.0 / 11.9 / 21.3px at 1050, so the tick's top wobbles between 13px and 46px from the row top down a single column of thirteen circles. Screenshotted at 768: TO DO, 'Mara & Finn' and 'High' all land level with line two of the note, not the title they belong to, which is the recorded lesson 'a person's words get the first line' inverted; nothing in interaction-check.mjs or the audit measures cross-axis alignment inside a row.

standing.element: .card[data-id^="seam_"] .cardTitle + .cardNote — the card the seam lands; guard at src/app.js:707
standing.problem: The one card the suite's signature gesture produces is the only card on the board whose note repeats its title verbatim. Driven at 1440x960: peel "Switch on before guests arrive, not when", Send to Tasks, Open in Tasks — the landed card in To do reads title "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" (14px/600 ink) then note "Switch on before guests arrive, not when." (13px/400 at 72% ink), the same sentence twice, differing only by a trailing full stop. The accessible layer says it twice too (aria-label plus the .sr summary). The author wrote the guard against exactly this and documented it ("a note that repeats its own title is noise") — src/app.js:707 compares entry.crossedWords.trim() !== String(entry.task).trim(), and the peeled words carry the sentence's own terminal period while the task-wording field does not, so a single "." defeats it. Every other card on the board earns its two lines ("Confirm marquee sides with the hire company" / "Mara & Finn, Saturday. Terrace plan if dry, marquee if not…").

One edit at src/app.js:707 clears the visible duplication AND the accessible one: task.note is in the sr describedby list at src/tasks.js:452 behind filter(Boolean), so an empty note drops it from the spoken summary too, leaving 'The house.' Card demo-t-03 already renders title-with-no-note, so the resulting shape is not an anomaly on this board.

(13px/400, 72% ink), and the sr summary at tasks.js:452 repeats it a third time — the guard at src/app.js:707 compares raw trimmed strings and the peel keeps the sentence-final period the task wording drops, so one '.' defeats a guard whose own comment forbids exactly this. It is NOT a distinct defect from seam-payoff-card-stutters, which is the same element, the same line and the same one-line fix; a fix round must collapse the two into a single edit.

standing.element: button.filingBtn[data-act="refile"] — labelled N.copy.filingLabel "Filing under" at src/notes.js:1796 (src/fixture.js:615) and hardcoded "What it is about" at src/notes.js:1878; aria-labels at src/notes.js:1741, 1881, 2180; destinationLabel "This task is filed under" at src/fixture.js:632; collides with button.groupBtn[data-act="group-about"] "What it is about" at src/notes.js:2106

standing.element: .card[aria-expanded] / .card[data-open] — src/tasks.js:52 declares `let openNoteId = null; /* the card showing its full note */`, read at src/tasks.js:428 (draggable), :430 (aria-expanded), :434 (data-open) and :2828 (Escape → "Note closed."); consumed by src/tasks.css:954, :956, :957, :1179, :1976
standing.problem: openNoteId is never assigned anything but null. Every one of the fourteen assignments in tasks.js (542, 554, 661, 2829, 2899, 3098, 3319, 3476, 3632, 4185, 4367) sets it to null; nothing sets it to a task id. Measured consequences: every card with a note ships a permanent `aria-expanded="false"`, `draggable` is permanently "true", `data-open` is never emitted, so five CSS rules can never match — including tasks.css:954 `.card[data-open] .cardNote { max-height: none }`, the rule that was supposed to release the five-line note clamp, and tasks.css:1179's open ring. The Escape branch at 2828-2832 (`say("Note closed.")`) is unreachable, so that sentence is in the build and can never be spoken. Driving it confirms the mechanism moved: a real mouse-down/up on `.cardTitle` opens `.taskPanel`, moves focus into it and announces "Task open." — the in-place disclosure the comment on line 52 describes does not exist. Separately, CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree on the card returns role=article with focusable/describedby/keyshortcuts/roledescription and NO `expanded` property at all: `aria-expanded` is not supported on role=article, so even a correct value would never reach a screen reader.
standing.fix: Delete the dead state, but do not delete the aria-expanded term wholesale: src/tasks.css:950 (`.card[aria-expanded]:hover .cardNote { color: var(--ink-1) }`) matches on attribute PRESENCE and is live today — it is what darkens a note under the pointer. Rewrite that selector to `.card:has(.cardNote):hover .cardNote` (or `.card[data-has-note]:hover`) in the same edit, then remove openNoteId, the aria-expanded and data-open terms, the Escape branch at 2834-2839, and the five CSS rules. While in there, .card[data-settling] (tasks.css:1252) is dead by the same test — data-settling is never written anywhere in tasks.js — so either revive it as the seam's arrival cue or remove it too.
standing.verdict: Verified line by line and by driving: all 14 writes to openNoteId in src/tasks.js (52, 550, 562, 669, 2837, 2907, 3106, 3328, 3485, 3641, 4194, 4382) assign null, so on tasks.board aria-expanded is only ever 'false', draggable only ever 'true', data-open count is 0, the five [data-open] rules (tasks.css 954, 956-957, 1179, 1976) can never match, and the Escape branch's 'Note closed.' is unreachable — pressing a card body opens .taskPanel and says 'Task open.'/'Task closed.' instead. CDP getPartialAXTree on the card returns role=article with focusable/describedby/keyshortcuts/roledescription and no expanded property, as claimed.

standing.element: [data-app="tasks"][data-density="compact"] .when — src/tasks.css:2167 `[data-app="tasks"][data-density="compact"] .when { height: 18px; font-size: 10.5px; ... }`; the state is switched at src/tasks.js:3204-3208 from the Show menu's Display row (src/tasks.js:800)
standing.problem: Compact is a real, one-click state — Show → Compact, `root.setAttribute("data-density", "compact")` — and sixteen CSS rules key off it, but it is not in elevate.config.json's `states` list, so neither gate ever visits it. Measured at 1440x960 with no scrolling (document scroll 0), after Send to Tasks the string 'Switch on before guests arrive, not when' is printed three times: .deskFactLink at (815,294) 13px/400 under the eyebrow IN TASKS AS, .peelSent at (272,445) 17px/600 under the eyebrow TASKS HAS IT, and a <b> at (264,667) 15px/400 in the ALREADY IN TASKS row. Two eyebrows name one fact two ways. Two separate controls both carry data-act="open-task" to the same destination, 233px apart — .deskFactLink at y=294 (accessible name 'Open in Tasks: Switch on before guests arrive, not when. Your note stays here.') and .act at y=527 ('Open in Tasks'). The reassurance is doubled too: .peelSent's 'Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit.' repeats the meta link's own 'Your note stays here.' Meanwhile the loudest rendering (17px/600) is the transient receipt and the durable record is the 13px/400 one, so prominence runs backwards. The same flow on a phone renders 2 occurrences and 1 control, which is the right shape — the duplication is desk-only, created by the meta column.
standing.fix: Do it with one guard, not three edits: at src/notes.js:1894 render the 'In Tasks as' .deskFact on `note.sent && !sentTask`, so while the receipt is up the margin row stands down entirely and returns the moment [data-act="close-peel"] clears sentTask — that removes the second printing, the second open-task control and the second reassurance together, and matches the shape the phone already has. Reject parts (a) and (c) of the proposed fix: keep the title in .peelSent (the receipt is where the eye is, and 'Tasks has it' alone names no object), and do not delete a visible sentence on the grounds that an accessible name carries it — that is moving truth out of the visible layer. Companion edit required: the send path deliberately focuses .deskFactLink (documented at src/notes.js:335), so retarget it to the receipt's own [data-act="open-task"] and keep the undo-revert refocus chain working.
standing.verdict: Every measurement checks out at 1280/1440/1920 with document scroll 0: after Send to Tasks the sentence prints at .deskFactLink (815,294) 13px/400 under eyebrow 'In Tasks as', .peelSent (272,445) 17px/600 under 'Tasks has it', and idxText b (264,667) 15px/400 under 'Already in Tasks'; two visible [data-act="open-task"] controls sit 233px apart with different accessible names to the same destination; and the phone renders the correct shape (one report, one control), so the desk meta column creates it. Driving it also shows focus after send landing on the quiet 13px margin link, not on the receipt's own 'Open in Tasks' 543px away — the duplication has a real cost, not just a tidiness one. This is the DISTINCT desk-duplication defect; seam-receipt-over-explains names the same pair from the copy side and adds nothing checkable, and it is a different defect from the card-note stutter that seam-card-repeats-its-own-title/seam-payoff-card-stutters name on the Tasks side.

standing.element: h1.headName in [data-app="notes"] .head, sibling of button.headNext[data-act="scope"] and button[data-act="unscope"] — src/notes.js (head template), src/notes.css (.headName)
standing.problem: Pressing .headNext cuts the index from 14 rows to 3. The index head honestly re-reads to '1 to decide / 3 notes', the scope button's accessible name honestly becomes 'Showing only these notes. Press to see the whole notebook.', and a filled release pill appears. But h1.headName — the one sentence that names what is on the sheet — keeps saying 'All your notes' (15px/400, 72% ink, x=549 at 1920) while 11 of 14 notes are hidden. 384px to its right the release pill reads 'All 14 notes' (data-act="unscope", x=933). So the head shows two near-identical phrases side by side, 'All your notes' and 'All 14 notes', and only the one that is a button is true; the true statement lives in the accessibility tree and not in the visible words. The visible on-state is otherwise a 2px indigo inset rule above the pressed words — a vocabulary Orla has no way to learn. Reproduces at 1280/1440/1920; the phone head does not render the h1 and is unaffected.
standing.fix: Key .headName off scope, but do not print the scope's own name in it: the pressed .headNext sits only 104px to its right already reading 'Mara & Finn', so 'Mara & Finn only' would repeat that name twice in one line. Render 'Your notes, narrowed' when scope is on (or simply drop the completeness word to 'Your notes') and restore 'All your notes' on unscope — the filled 'x All 14 notes' pill is already the visible release. Keep the head count-free per the standing decision. Assert in interaction-check.mjs that after pressing [data-act="scope"] h1.headName no longer contains 'All your notes'.
standing.verdict: Reproduced at 1280/1440/1920: pressing [data-act="scope"] cuts .idxRow from 14 to 3 and the index head honestly re-reads '1 to decide / 3 notes', but h1.headName stays the hard-coded 'All your notes' (src/notes.js:1628) 384px left of a filled ink release pill reading 'All 14 notes' — the element that names the sheet is the only thing in the head still asserting completeness, and the narrowing is stated only in the scope button's aria-label and a 2px indigo inset rule.

standing.element: [data-app="tasks"] .card .cardNote in the board view between 1100 and 1279px — the board/list crossing at 1100 (src/tasks.js) and the tray floor (src/tasks.css .tray min/max width)
standing.problem: There is a 180px-wide band where the board is kept and its cards stop saying what to do. Measured on tasks.dense: at 1280 zero of eight card notes are trimmed; at 1279 all eight are, and at 1100 the notes render 18-45 per cent of their text in 196px lanes. 'Add Northlight (photography) and County Marquee. Drop the lapsed DJ.' renders as 'Add Northlight (photography)…' at every width from 1100 to 1279 — the instruction is the part that is gone. 'Top table moved away from the speakers, check sightlines to the arch.' renders 23 per cent at 1180. At 1100 one card title is trimmed as well. The board's own two automated loops straddle this exactly: five lanes are proved to FIT at 1180, and a note is proved to READ IN FULL only at 1280 and 1440, so nothing checks reading at 1180. The list view that solves it already exists and is switched on 1px lower, at 1099, where the same notes are read whole. Trims are whole-word and the full string is in the accessible name, so this costs a screen-reader user nothing and costs sighted Orla the content of every card.
standing.fix: The diagnosis is right and the remedy is oversized. Lane width at 1279 is 226px and the note measure 149px — identical to 1280 — so the entire cliff is the `@media (min-width: 1280px)` max-height override at src/tasks.css:946-949, not the lane. Patched live: releasing the 5-line cap alone gives 0 of 9 notes and 0 of 9 titles trimmed at 1279 with the board still fitting (0px over). So move that media query's floor to 1200 rather than moving the board/list crossing to 1280 — the proposed 1280 crossing would delete the board across a band where interaction-check.mjs itself asserts 'board @1180 · five lanes fit with nothing sliced', turning a green assertion red. Below 1200 the lane is genuinely too narrow (4 of 9 titles still trim at 1180, 9 of 9 at 1100, board 30px over at 1100), so raise the crossing from 1099 to 1199 — the same threshold the sheet already stamps data-head=stack at — and extend the note loop to [1200, 1279, 1280, 1440].
standing.verdict: Measured on tasks.dense: 8 of 9 card notes carry the word-safe ellipsis at 1279, 1180 and 1100 and 0 of 9 at 1280; at 1100 all 9 titles trim too, and at 1099 the list view (.listBoard/.lrowNote) shows zero ellipses. interaction-check.mjs really does straddle it — lane fit loops [1180,1280,1366,1440], note reading only [1280,1440] — so nothing checks reading at 1180.

standing.element: [data-app="tasks"] .tray[data-lane] .trayBody[data-more] and the .tray::after fold rule — src/tasks.css:812-827, set by measureEdges() at src/tasks.js:3761
standing.problem: In the state built to test density, 10 of 32 tasks are hidden and nothing on the sheet says so in words. At 1920x1000 on tasks.dense the To Do scroller runs 195-775 and its fifth card ends at exactly 775, so no card peeks; '+ Add here' sits at 779, four pixels below the cut, in the position that conventionally terminates a list. Five tasks — 'Price the extra hour on the bar for Nora & Cian', 'Send Aisling & Tom the autumn pricing sheet', 'Pencil the autumn date in the diary', 'Service the terrace heaters before October', 'Replace the two broken chairs in the barn' — are entirely below it. In Progress hides 2 of 7 and Done 3 of 9. The scrollbar gutter is 0px, there is no mask. The two cues are a 1px rule at rgba(17,17,17,0.08) — the identical --line token every card border is drawn in — and the numeral 10 at 11px/400/62 per cent ink, 630px away at the far right of the lane head, which requires Orla to count the visible cards and subtract. The fold rule was chosen over a gradient for a good rendering reason recorded in the CSS; the gap it leaves is that the cue carries no word.
standing.fix: Two corrections to the proposal. (1) Fix the cue as well as the word: a hairline drawn in the same --line value as every card border cannot read as a cue whatever it says beside it — step the fold to --ink-4, the value the card's own open ring already uses, so it is a different line from the thirty it sits among. (2) Do not add a button. Three lanes gaining a second tab stop in their foot, and 'Add here' pushed a row further down, costs more than it buys; render the residue as quiet non-interactive text in the trayAdd row's own line ('5 more below', 13px/400/62% ink, right-aligned) and let the existing lane scroller and card rover do the moving. Derive the number as lane count minus fully-visible cards from the same accessor the head count uses, and assert it in interaction-check.mjs at 1920 and 1440.
standing.verdict: Every measurement checks out on tasks.dense at 1920x1000: To Do body runs 195-775 with 5 of 10 cards fully visible, 0 partially visible (no peek), and 'Add here' at 779; In Progress hides 2 of 7, Done 3 of 9 — 10 of 32 in all. The tray::after fold computes to rgba(17,17,17,0.08), the identical value the card border is drawn in, mask-image is none and the scrollbar gutter is 0. A full text scan of [data-app="tasks"] finds no element containing 'more', 'below', 'hidden' or 'of 10', and .trayBody carries no aria-label, so neither a sighted nor a screen-reader user is told anything — the only cue is the lane total 630px up at 11px/400/62% ink, which has to be reconciled by counting and subtracting.

refuted.problem: One app, one Ctrl Z, three different promises about the way back — measured by driving, not read. Notes writes "Sent to Tasks. Undo [Ctrl Z] for 30 seconds" in a dark 317x46 pill and ticks the number down every second (30 -> 23 at t=7s -> 15 at t=15s -> "for 1 seconds" at t=29s -> gone at t=32s). Tasks writes "<Title> done" — no verb, no full stop, no window — in the same dark pill and silently retires it between t=5.5s and t=7.0s (6000ms, src/tasks.js:2348), while its announcement says only "Press Ctrl Z to undo." Timeline writes "Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days earlier." in a 1096x64 WHITE bar inline in the sheet at y=514 and it is still there at t=35s; it never expires. So a person who learns in Notes that the offer lasts 30 counted seconds ticks a task, looks away, and finds the way back gone at 6 with nothing having said so. Three grammars for one event as well: bare adjective, verb-only, full sentence — and Tasks runs five internally ("<T> done", "<T> is not done", "<T> added to Review", "<T> moved to Done", "<T> is due Friday"). The one ticking number also reads "for 1 seconds" for its last full second (src/notes.js:288), in a codebase that otherwise pluralises carefully ("1 word picked.", "1 character over").
refuted.why: Driven at 1920, the harm story is inverted. The 6000ms at src/tasks.js:2357 retires the STRIP, not the offer — its own comment says so ('The strip retires; the record does not') and undoHistory holds ten acts: I ticked 'Confirm marquee sides with the hire company', watched the pill go between t=5.6s and t=8.1s, pressed Ctrl+Z at t=15.7s and the card came back out of Done (6 to 5 cards) with the live region announcing 'is back in the to do column'. Timeline's white bar is likewise still live and still working at t=36.7s. The one product where the way back is genuinely taken away is NOTES — the seam's peel at t=33.7s, past the counter, left the Tasks board at 14 cards and Ctrl+Z did nothing — which is the product the finding holds up as the honest standard and whose 30-second expiry it proposes hoisting into the other two, i.e. the fix would delete a ten-deep never-expiring undo in Tasks and a permanent one in Timeline to install the only expiry in the suite. There are two behaviours here, not three promises, and the finding names the wrong one as the trap.

refuted.problem: One press of Send to Tasks, and at 1440x960 the same sentence prints three times inside 373px of vertical span — "Switch on before guests arrive, not when" at 13px/400 under "IN TASKS AS", at 17px/600 under "TASKS HAS IT", and at 15px/400 under "ALREADY IN TASKS". Four labels claim the same fact ("In Tasks as", "Tasks has it", "Already in Tasks", "Sent to Tasks.") and the reassurance is said four times in four wordings: "Your note stays here." (the sheet, before), "Your note is still here, still private, still yours to edit." (the receipt), "…and every note stayed here" (the index head), "Your note stayed here." (the live region). Saying the one thing a person might doubt four times reads anxious, which is the opposite of the register this surface holds everywhere else.
refuted.why: Not a distinct defect: its one checkable observation — 'In Tasks as' in the margin and 'Tasks has it' in the receipt reporting one fact at once — is exactly what seam-landing-reported-four-ways already names, with better evidence and the same single guard, so confirming it would fix one thing twice. Its added counts do not survive measurement: of the four labels, 'Already in Tasks' is the section head over four ledger rows and 'Sent to Tasks.' is the undo strip's own label naming what would be reverted; of the four reassurances, .peelBoundary is the pre-commit contract and is gone the instant the receipt replaces the peel (measured at 1440: only .peelWhy and the ledger .cnt are on screen after send), and the aria-live line is the receipt's accessibility channel, not a fifth voice. Three of its four edits would make the work worse — shortening the live region drops 'In The house.', the destination, from the only channel an AT user gets it in at that moment; cutting the ledger head to a bare '4 so far' trades a standing sentence for a naked count on the surface whose recorded decision is that counts are not its loudest object; and putting the wording on the undo pill would add a FIFTH printing of the sentence the finding is complaining about.

refuted.problem: The one object that is identical in all three products — the 17px/600 product wordmark with the indigo full stop — is the one object that moves when you change product. Measured from the shared white sheet's own top edge (all three sheets are the same box, 100,18): the wordmark's optical centre sits 31.0px down in Notes and 30.0px down in Tasks, and 52.8px down in Timeline. That is a 22px drop, identical at 1280, 1440 and 1920, plus a 12px shift right (28px inset in Tasks, 40px in Timeline) and a taller line box (25.5px vs 22.0px). Driving the rail from Tasks to Timeline, the indigo accent glides between slots as one liquid band — genuinely the best 200ms in the suite — and in the same beat the identity lurches down and right. The thing that should be nailed to the sheet is the thing that slides, which is the specific tell that reads as three sites behind one rail rather than one application.
refuted.why: This and wordmark-first-baseline-drifts-22px-on-timeline are ONE defect reported twice — same span.word, same cause (--stage-pad top plus --lead-body), same widths, differing only in datum (optical centre vs first baseline) — and the identity-drops-on-the-timeline-crossing reasoning kills both: measured at the wordmark's own left, the only two boxes aligned below Timeline's mark are div.tl-stage and section.b-field, so its 40px top is the same page inset as its 40px left, exactly as Tasks' mark sits on the 28px its trayHead/trayTop/pip/segItem resolve to and Notes' sits on the stack's own edge. The centres reproduce (30.00 / 31.01 / 52.75 at 1920 and 1440), but the alignment being defended is not a contract: driven at six widths the Tasks-Notes gap is 0.13px at 1920 and 1440, 0.87px at 1280 and 1100, 10.95px at 768, and 5.87px at 390 — where Timeline's wordmark already sits 8px ABOVE Tasks', so raising it makes the phone worse. And the finding's premise that this is 'the one object nailed to the sheet' is contradicted by its own concession: Notes' wordmark stands 371px from the sheet edge at 1920, 131 at 1440, 51 at 1280, 16 at 390, a 355px horizontal slide the finding calls defensible. The fix is also unwritable as specified: var(--lead-tight) exists in neither timeline.css nor across.css, and Timeline's declared ladder (0.9 / 1.06 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 / 1.5, 'six steps... audit.mjs fails a leading that is not one of them') has no step yielding a 22px box at 17px.

refuted.problem: The uppercase micro-label — the object that says 'this names a region', and the most repeated typographic unit in the suite — renders at five specs, split cleanly along the old product borders. Measured at 1920 across eight states: Tasks is Geist Mono 11px/400, +0.10em, leading 14px; Timeline is Geist Mono 11px/400, +0.16em, leading 15.4px (plus 12px/400 +0.20em on h1.b-who); Notes is Geist 11px/600, +0.075em, leading 15.95px, and 12px/600 +0.075em on .darkTag. So walking the spine from TO DO to DAYS AWAY changes the label's letterfit by 60% (1.1px vs 1.76px of tracking at the same 11px), and walking to FILING UNDER changes its family and its weight as well. Three separate declarations exist for one role: --tr-cap: 0.075em (notes.css:108), a hard 0.1em literal (tasks.css:777 and :1104), --track-label: 0.16em (timeline.css:67). The audit gate already reports this and does not pass it: 'Geist Mono|11|label → 1.1px vs 1.76px  h2.trayName "To do" | span "one of three"'. The suite's own claim is one application; the label tier is the place a reader can see the seam.
refuted.why: The census reproduces exactly at 1920 across eight states (Tasks 11/400 +0.10em/14px on 11 of 11 labels; Timeline 11/400 +0.16em/15.4px on every label with h1.b-who's +0.20em declared separately; Notes 11/600 +0.075em/15.95px, .darkTag 12px), but it shows three internally flawless systems, not drift: zero within-product variance, no uppercase micro-label anywhere in the shell chrome, and the other two apps at display:none, so the three specs are never co-present — the seam is a memory across a rail crossing, not a mismatch on screen. The remedy is where it fails: --track-label: 0.14em is a value no product ratified, and it simultaneously overrules Tasks' written one-rule (tasks.css:770-778, '+0.1em... tracking carries the hierarchy, so a small label is never bolded to make it matter') and Timeline's written ladder (timeline.css:66-68, 'five different values on 11px uppercase mono... six steps and no seventh'), while --label-face/--label-weight convert Notes' most-repeated label from Geist 600 to Geist Mono 400 at rgba(17,17,17,0.62) — rendered at 4x, 'FILING UNDER' goes visibly lighter and machine-set on the one product whose direction is paper. COMPOSITION.md §0-1 records the argued refusal to reconcile any type token across the three ('each is a value a panel settled inside a room'), and the finding's own stated ground — 'the audit gate already reports this and does not pass it' — is false: gate.mjs exits 0 with tracking declared, reported and ungated.

refuted.problem: Round 5 flagged this and it was not changed, so here is the measurement, taken at 1920 with all three sheets starting at exactly (100, 18). The wordmark's FIRST BASELINE sits 36.00px below the sheet's top edge in Tasks and 36.13px below it in Notes — a 0.13px agreement, which is a real contract, not a coincidence. In Timeline it sits 58.00px below: the same 17px/600 word, 22px lower. Horizontally Tasks puts it 28px in from the sheet's leading edge (tasks.css:257 states that 28px IS the sheet's one leading edge, shared with the view pill, the tray label and every card) and Timeline puts it 40px in (--stage-pad). The mechanical cause of part of the drop is a leading error: the wordmark takes line-height: var(--lead-body), and --lead-body is declared at timeline.css:94 as '1.5 · all prose, 13 to 20px' — a prose leading on a wordmark, giving 25.5px against Tasks' declared 22px and Notes' 21.76px. Three leadings on one object. This matters more in a suite than it did in three standalone products: the wordmark is the ONE element whose entire job is to hold still while the word inside it changes, so that switching the spine reads as a change of label rather than a re-layout. Driving the spine Tasks → Timeline, the identity jumps 22px down and 12px right, and it is the only thing on the head that moves.
refuted.why: Same object and same cause as wordmark-drops-when-you-change-product — one defect, reported twice, and the two disagree with each other on the remedy (that one keeps the 40px left 'because it is the stage's real left edge', this one moves it to 28px), which is itself evidence that no single violated rule exists. The baselines reproduce exactly (36.00 tasks / 36.13 notes / 58.00 timeline, relative to a sheet at 100,18) but the '0.13px agreement, a real contract, not a coincidence' holds at two of six driven widths: 0.13 at 1920 and 1440, 0.87 at 1280 and 1100, 10.95 at 768, and 5.87 at 390 where Timeline is already 8px ABOVE Tasks — two independently chosen head tokens (a 60px centred bar, a 10px pad on a 62px min-height) landing near each other twice, not a rule. The leading claim is also wrong in kind: Timeline's ladder bands those steps by SIZE ('1.5 · all prose, 13 to 20px', '1.2 · 24, 30, 38px', '1.06 · 48px and up'), so a 17px mark on --lead-body is the ladder obeyed, while the proposed hard 22px is 1.294 — the undeclared seventh step the file's own comment says audit.mjs fails. Moving the head to 28px would take the mark off div.tl-stage and section.b-field, the only two boxes that share its left edge, and the finding's own phone re-check (19px var(--gap-line)) lands Timeline at ~35px against Tasks' 42 and Notes' 36.13, leaving the three-way disagreement it set out to close.

refuted.problem: The lane caption is the only text block in Tasks with no widow control — computed text-wrap is `wrap`, greedy — and its reserve is one line (min-height: 1.4em = 16.8px). tasks.css:907 names this exact omission as 'the real objection' when arguing the cardTitle rule, and then leaves it in place on the caption. Measured at 1920 and 1440, on the shipped board: the collapsed WAITING lane is 172px wide against the others' 372px, so its 43-character caption wraps to two lines and rags to a three-word runt, 'or a decision.' Its caption bottom is 200px against 183px for the other four, and its first content item sits at y=227 against y=197 — the five lane heads stand on two baselines and the head row of the board is visibly ragged in the delivered 1920 frame. It gets worse in the 1100-1179 band, which no gate width covers: at 1100, REVIEW's caption also goes to two lines and WAITING's to three, so the first cards stand at 298 (To do, In progress, Done), 314 (Review) and lower still (Waiting) — three baselines on five lanes at the last width where the board is still a board. The collapse of an empty lane is a designed decision; its typographic consequence was not.
refuted.why: The CSS facts hold (computed text-wrap: wrap, min-height 16.8px) but the consequences are overstated and the fix, applied in-page and re-measured, fails its own claim: all five .trayName heads sit at y=145 exactly at 1920 and the four populated lanes' first cards all sit at 196.8 — only the deliberately collapsed empty WAITING lane's empty-state line is lower (226.6), and after `min-height: calc(1.4em*2)` the four card lanes drop to 213.6 while WAITING stays at 226.6, so the rag the finding leads with survives the fix while every board from 1100 up pays 16.8px of permanent head height. The band is also mis-stated: at 1140 and 1160 every caption except the collapsed lane is one line, so the two-card-baseline case lives in roughly 1100-1129, and at 1100 WAITING still takes three lines against a two-line reserve. `balance` is not free either — it trades 'or a decision.' for a line ending on the article 'a' split from 'delivery' ('Held by a reply, a / delivery, or a decision.'), while `pretty` changes the 1920 break not at all.

refuted.problem: tasks.css:288-291 writes the suite's rule down in the file: 'The sheet's own title is the largest thing on it. Four sizes inside a 2px band, all at 600, gave the top of the scale no rank at all.' Measured in the 60-66px head band at 1920, one product of three keeps it. Tasks: h1 'The Orchard, events' at 20px/600 in ink-1 is the largest text on the sheet head, 3px above the wordmark — clean, one title, one rank. Notes: the same class on the same element is 15px/400 in ink-2, so the h1 'All your notes' is the THIRD-ranked object in its own head, out-ranked by span.word 'notes' at 17px/600 and tied on size but beaten on weight by the sibling button.headNext b 'Mara & Finn' at 15px/600. The largest word on the Notes sheet head is the product's own name; the largest word on the Tasks sheet head is the venue. Timeline puts its h1 (h1.b-who 'Mara & Finn') at 12px/400 Geist Mono uppercase — the smallest text in the product. So a person walking the spine gets three different answers to 'which word on this head tells me where I am', and in Notes the answer is a 15px grey label sitting between two darker, heavier neighbours, with a 100px gap and no size step to separate the h1 from the toggle beside it. That is the one thing a shared head has to get right, and the rule to get it right is already written in the repo.
refuted.why: The type ranks are measured correctly (Tasks h1 20px/600 ink-1 over a 17px wordmark; Notes h1.headName 15px/400 at 72% ink behind span.word 17px/600 and button.headNext b 15px/600; Timeline h1.b-who 12px/400 mono) but the argument and fix fail: at 1920 the h1's right edge is 644 and the toggle's left is 657, a 13px gap not the claimed 100px, and a .headRule separates the wordmark from the h1/fact pair, so there is no unseparated tie; Timeline's b-who is not 'the smallest text in the product' (b-measureHead and b-behindLabel are 11px). The fix would make a filter control (aria-pressed, narrows the notebook) the sheet's 20px/600 h1 while demoting the only element that names the sheet's scope to a 13px span, and would invent a second 20px/600 title in a head whose title object the finding itself concedes is the founder-locked 148px number.

refuted.problem: This is the paid-for library's "the measure has a floor AND a ceiling" defect, back with the same trigger and almost the same number. Drove Planning open at 1440x960: the sheet goes 1322 -> 916, lanes go 280 -> 196, the card goes 256 -> 172 and .cardNote's measure goes 202px -> 118px — about 17 characters a line. Counted the damage: with the drawer shut, 0 of 13 card titles and 0 of 13 notes are clipped; with it open, 4 of 13 titles clip ('Reprint the faded welcome sign before the open...', 'Send midweek rate to the June 2027 walk-in...', 'Clear Sunday 11am late checkout...', 'Send registrar paperwork two...') and 'Menu tasting at The Orchard' loses its note's operative clause to the five-line cap, while its 27-character title now breaks over three lines. Same at 1280 (sheet 756, note 118px). Orla opens Planning to plan against the board, and the act of opening it takes a third of the board's words away. The trims themselves are clean — whole-word, full string in the aria-label — so nothing is lied about; the composition just stops being legible at a width no frame covers. The floor that fixes it is already written in this file, 9 lines above the drawer rule, keyed to a viewport query the drawer can never trigger.
refuted.why: The measurements reproduce exactly (1440: sheet 1322->916, lanes 280->196, card 256->172, note 202->118, the same four titles trimmed, and 'Menu tasting' losing 'before service notes are locked'), but the diagnosis inverts the paid lesson: 196 IS the declared floor (src/tasks.css:633 `--lane: minmax(196px, 372px)`), applied deliberately with the drawer open and recorded there, not an undocumented collapse to 105px — and 'Panels that open must not delete columns' is honoured as shipped (Done shows 180px of itself, board overflow 32px with the snap already on .tray) while the proposed fix violates it. Driven with the rule in place before render at 1440-planning, `repeat(5, minmax(258px,1fr))` puts Done 132px PAST the board's right edge (doneShown -132, overflow 406px), failing the standing assertion 'planning open @1440 · Done is still on the board, not deleted by the drawer' by 228px, and because data-head="stack" is stamped at sheet<1200 it also breaks 'five lanes fit with nothing sliced' for the drawer-SHUT board at 1180 (260px over) and 1280 (160px over). refuted.problem: The suite's argument is that nothing rebuilds when you cross the rail, and the wordmark on the sheet's own head is the object that proves it. It does not hold still. Clicked .rail [data-rail="notes|tasks|timeline"] round-trip at 1920x1000 and re-measured span.word on every crossing (stable and repeatable): box top y=37.0 for tasks and y=38.1 for notes — the two agree to 1.1px — and y=58.0 for timeline. Timeline's word also sits on 25.5px leading against 22px and 21.76px, so its baseline lands 22.8px lower and the box bottom moves 59.0 / 59.9 / 83.5. Clicking Timeline visibly drops the identity and clicking back lifts it, which is the one motion the architecture promises will not happen. The same padding also spends a 66px band on one 70px word and then builds a second head (div.b-bar, 56px, carrying the project name and the three acts) 40px beneath it, where tasks and notes carry identity, project, facts and actions on one 60-62px line. The horizontal difference (128 / 471 / 140) is defensible — each wordmark aligns to its own product's measure. The vertical is aligned to nothing.
refuted.why: The numbers reproduce exactly (word box top 37.0 tasks / 38.13 notes / 58.0 timeline, stable over five rail round-trips at 1920/1440/1280), but the finding's load-bearing claim — 'the vertical is aligned to nothing... nothing but padding puts it there' — is false: .tlHead's top padding is var(--stage-pad)=40px, the same single token that produces the horizontal inset the finding itself concedes is defensible, and it lands the wordmark at the page's own 40/40 inset corner (word left 140 = .b-ownerField stage left 140, sheet origin 100,18). All three verticals are governed by each product's own head token exactly as all three horizontals are (tasks centred in a 60px bar, notes in a 62px min-height bar, timeline at the page inset), so the finding calls one axis principled and the identical logic on the other axis arbitrary. The 'one motion the architecture promises will not happen' also misreads the locked promise, which is that no product is ever torn down, not that chrome shares a baseline; and the fix's literal `padding: 19px 40px 0` collides with the `--stage-pad: 0px` phone rule at src/timeline.css:384 and the ≤430px .tlHead override at src/across.css:423.

refuted.problem: The empty lane yielding its width is a decision, stated in the comment at :1782. The prose staying full-width inside the yielded track is not. Measured at 1920x1000: To do / In progress / Review / Done are 372px each, their .trayNote sits on one 17px line, .trayHead is 50px, and all four first cards start at y=197. Waiting is pinned to 172px, so 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.' wraps to two lines (34px), its .trayHead is 67px, and its only content starts at y=227 — 30px below the four cards beside it. Constant at 1680, 1440 and 1280 (172px every time), and worse with Planning open at 1440: Waiting drops to 132px with a THREE-line note (head 83px, content at y=344) while Review wraps to two (head 67px, y=314) and the rest hold 50px/298 — three head heights and three first-row baselines in one five-lane row, spanning 46px. The proof that it is fallout and not intent: the phone board, where every lane is 299px, renders all five notes on one line with all five heads at 50px, and the tasks.dense state at 1920, where Waiting is populated and its note fits one line at 372px. The row of five lane heads is the strongest horizontal line on the board, and it is the one line that does not hold.
refuted.why: Every number reproduces (1920: four heads at 49.8px with first cards at 196.8, Waiting pinned to 172px with a two-line note, head 66.6px, its content at 226.6; 172px constant at 1680/1440/1280; Planning open at 1440 giving three head heights 49.8/66.6/83.4 and a 46.6px spread), but the diagnosis and the remedy both fail. The wrap is not undeclared fallout: the same comment the finding cites for the yield says at src/tasks.css:631-632 that an empty lane becomes a rail because 'its sentence and its Add row still fit' — the sentence staying in the head is the stated decision, and it fits without clipping. Driven, the proposed fix does the opposite of what it promises: hiding .trayNote drops the yielded head to 26px, not 50, so two head heights remain and the first rows are still 10.8px apart at 1920 (27.6px at 1440 with Planning, where three head heights survive), while the relocated sentence runs to five lines in the 172px rail and seven lines in the 132px track. Nor is 'one baseline' reachable this way: equalising the heads with a two-line reserve still leaves 13px, because .trayEmpty is not a card and does not sit on a card's top edge — the finding is comparing four card edges with one empty-state sentence in a lane that has no card. Review, a populated 196px lane, wraps to two lines too, so a two-line caption is a property of a narrow track rather than of yielding.
